stemMd: A data set consists of $12$ test scores with a mean of $78$. If the lowest score is removed from the data set, the mean of the remaining $11$ scores is $81$. If instead the highest score is removed from the original data set, the mean of the remaining $11$ scores is $76$. What is the range of the original $12$ scores?
explanationMd:
Means are easiest to work with as **totals**: total $=$ mean $\times$ number of values.

- All $12$ scores: $12 \times 78 = 936$.
- Without the lowest score: $11 \times 81 = 891$, so the lowest score is $936 - 891 = 45$.
- Without the highest score: $11 \times 76 = 836$, so the highest score is $936 - 836 = 100$.

The range is the highest score minus the lowest:

$$100 - 45 = 55$$

There is also a one-line route. The highest score minus the lowest score equals (total without the lowest) minus (total without the highest), because the remaining $10$ scores cancel:

$$11 \times 81 - 11 \times 76 = 11 \times 5 = 55$$

Check that such a data set can exist: the other $10$ scores total $936 - 45 - 100 = 791$, a mean of $79.1$, which sits comfortably between $45$ and $100$.

The trap is to work with the means directly. The two reduced means differ by $5$, but each is a mean of $11$ scores, so the totals differ by $11 \times 5$, not $5$ and not $12 \times 5$.

distractorRationale.a: This is the difference between the two reduced means, $81 - 76$. Each mean is of $11$ scores, so the corresponding totals, and hence the two removed scores, differ by $11 \times 5 = 55$.
distractorRationale.c: This multiplies the difference in means by $12$, the size of the original data set. The two reduced means are each of $11$ scores, so the factor is $11$.
distractorRationale.d: This is the highest score, $936 - 836 = 100$. The range subtracts the lowest score, $45$, from it.

accessibilityText: Twelve test scores have a mean of 78. Removing the lowest score leaves 11 scores with a mean of 81. Removing instead the highest score leaves 11 scores with a mean of 76. What is the range of the 12 scores? The choices are 5, 55, 60 and 100.

provenance.notes: Original item. Recovers the extreme values of a data set from how the mean changes when each is removed; the insight is that both reduced totals share the same 10 scores.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Sum = 12*78 = 936; lowest = 936 - 11*81 = 45; highest = 936 - 11*76 = 100; range = 55. 5 is the difference of means, 100 is the max, 60 is a miscalculation. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-sat-math-run1) reached the same answer: Total = 936; removing lowest leaves 891 so lowest = 45; removing highest leaves 836 so highest = 100; range = 55. 5 is the difference of means; 60 and 100 misuse the values.]
